title: Ops Concierge Differentiation Lab: Field Scenarios & Objection Scripts
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a field-facing tactic pack that reframes Redwood as an "ops concierge" for inference — aimed at platform teams, SREs, and infra-driven product leads who care less about single-model FOMO and more about predictable SLOs, measurable unit economics, and operational safety. Use for AE prep, SDR handoffs, and SE sparring.

One-liner positioning to open a call:
"Redwood is the inference control plane that lets your platform own SLAs, routing, and cost — without rebuilding a pile of custom schedulers or sacrificing latency when traffic spikes."

Why this angle works (sales thesis):
- Platform buyers rarely buy on model name alone; they buy on operational guarantees (latency, isolation, rollouts, cost predictability).
- Competitors tout model access and simple APIs; we win by mapping those promises to real ops outcomes (fewer incidents, lower tail-cost, faster rollback).
- Conversation becomes about runbooks + economics instead of model benchmarks, which reduces comparison to vendor marketing.

Primary pain signals to probe for (discovery questions):
- "How do you measure latency SLOs for external-facing endpoints today? Where do you see most violations?"
- "What’s your current strategy for failover when capacity is constrained? Any manual escalations?"
- "Who owns the cost curve for tokens/embedding compute? Are token spikes tied to feature launches?"
- "Have you done canary rollouts for model upgrades? How long does a rollback take?"

Field scenario scripts (three prescriptive vignettes):
1) Platform Team at Series B SaaS — "Spiky billing and SLA anxiety"
- Pain: Sudden user growth causing cost and latency spikes; finance surprises.
- Win script: Emphasize Redwood’s routing by policy (priority queues), automatic KV/prefix caching, and per-route token breakdowns in Console. Offer a quick cost model: estimate 60% token cost reduction from prefix caching + batching for chat-heavy workflows.
- Demo hook: Show per-route latency histograms + token cost waterfall, and a 5-minute policy change (move route to lower-cost region with auto-fallback).

2) Enterprise regulated customer — "Compliance + private deployment"
- Pain: Need VPC, KMS, and audited rollback for model logic in pipelines.
- Win script: Walk through Redwood Private (control plane with customer-managed network), KMS integration, and audit logs. Highlight that model pinning + rollout policies mean legal can approve a specific model artifact and ops can control release windows.
- Demo hook: Show audit trail for a model rollout and a simulated rollback.

3) Data platform team — "Embedded inference at scale"
- Pain: Machine teams want high throughput embeddings and occasional low-latency generations; different SLAs across workloads.
- Win script: Present Dedicated capacity pools, autoscale/burst settings, and workload-aware kernel selection. Show math on reserving a small Dedicated pool for embeddings to cut latency 4x vs noisy shared endpoints.
- Demo hook: Attach a throughput dashboard and a reserved capacity plan (monthly commit v. burst usage).

Competitive traps and concise rebuttals (quick lines your AE/SE can use):
- Trap: "We can self-host and save money long-term."
  - Rebuttal: "Self-hosting saves on list price but hides ops tax: scheduling, KV cache correctness, continuous batching, and tail latency debugging. Our customers report ~3x faster time-to-stable and significantly lower incident MTTR once they move serving to Redwood’s runtime. We’ll share a migration checklist that isolates the actual engineering effort so you can compare apples-to-apples."

- Trap: "We only care about model fidelity; cheaper quantized variants degrade quality."
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood Optimize ties quantization suggestions to your eval sets. We recommend quantization profiles per route based on measured quality regressions — not a blanket swap. That gets you cost benefits with guardrails."

- Trap: "Vendor X has more model choices."
  - Rebuttal: "Model breadth is helpful, but model compatibility and consistent latency are what operational teams care about. Our smart-routing policies and verified model profiles reduce risk during scale and make multi-model fallbacks predictable."

Technical objection handling (detailed):
- Objection: "How do you handle cold-starts and KV cache invalidation for chat?"
- Response: "Our runtime maintains per-customer KV caching and prefix caching; we provide TTL and cache-control hooks so you can treat cache warming as part of rollout automation. For cold-starts we support warm pools and pre-warming scripts in Dedicated deployments."
  - Quick proof: We can demo a cold-start/steady-state latency curve and show where caching reduces median+tail latency."

- Objection: "We need audited encryption at rest with HSM-backed keys."
  - Response: "Private supports KMS/HSM integrations with audit trails and key rotation. SEs and security can review our reference architecture and the evidence pack (SOC2 artifacts + audit snippets)."

Economics quick math (prep for price pushback):
- Fast formula (chat-heavy app):
  - Baseline tokens/month = active users * avg-requests/user/day * avg-tokens/request * 30
  - Cost drivers we control: batching efficiency (% tokens saved), prefix cache savings, model routing to cheaper variants during bulk processing.
- Example anchor: 100k MAU, 0.5 requests/day, 250 tokens/request => ~3.75B tokens/month. Typical optimization (good batching + caching + routing) can reduce effective billable tokens by 30–60% depending on conversation shape.

Demo checklist (what to show in a 15-min technical demo):
- Per-route latency + cost waterfall (Console)
- Model pinning + canary rollout (show rollback)
- Live two-region failover (simulate region down)
- Dedicated pool autoscale and burst behavior (throughput view)
- Optimize suggestion for a target route (quantization/batching hint)

Hand-offs and escalation signals (for AE -> SE -> Solutions Eng):
- Handoff trigger: prospect asks for SLOs or dedicated capacity, or requests an architecture review — include traffic profile CSV + current incident postmortem if available.
- Escalation signals: unable to commit to <100ms p50 latency across x path, insistence on HSM smoke test, or unusual embedding throughput (>200 qps sustained) request.
- Packaging for SE: attach usage sample, target SLOs, list of regulatory constraints, and an example prompt set for evals.

Slack-ready bite snippets (use these verbatim in threads):
- Win opener: "We help platform teams own latency and cost so PMs ship features without surprise infra bills."
- Objection nuke: "Totally fair — self-hosting hides an ops tax. We’ll give you the migration checklist and three case studies to compare the real run rate."

Next steps templates (for AE to send after discovery):
1) Short follow-up email + CTA to schedule an SE workshop (attach usage CSV).
2) Offer a 2-week pilot plan: small dedicated pool, two prioritized routes, and an eval set to measure quality regression.
3) Use a lightweight contract framework: 30-day pilot + optional month-to-month Dedicated commit.

Open questions / runbook items to finalize with SEs:
- Standard pilot SLA matrix and what incident telemetry we’ll expose.
- Typical engineering scope for private deployment (networking checklist).
- Example eval sets for common verticals (support chat, search rerank, embeddings).

Notes to self (fragments for future revisions):
- Add a short one-pager quantifying MTTR improvements customers reported after switching to Redwood.
- Collect three anonymized cost-savings case studies focused on prefix caching results.
- Draft a canned SE demo script for embedding throughput comparison (shared vs Dedicated).

Use this as a practical, ops-first scriptbook for reps who need to move conversations away from model soup and into measurable operational outcomes.
